The core insight is that team success depends not only on individual talent but also on how well player types complement each other. This leads to a dual framework: first, identifying distinct player roles through clustering of behavioral data; second, modeling team outcomes as functions of these role combinations. The mathematical duality lies between the discrete assignment of players to roles and the continuous evaluation of their synergistic effects. Failure modes include misclassification of player roles leading to incorrect clustering, and ignoring confounding variables such as coaching quality. The system must dynamically adjust its belief about team fit based on empirical performance data, using Bayesian updating to refine role assignments and outcome predictions.
